definition: A capsule neural network (CapsNet) is a machine learning system that is a type of artificial neural network (ANN) that can be used to better model hierarchical relationships.
details: The approach is an attempt to more closely mimic biological neural organization. The idea is to add structures called "capsules" to a convolutional neural network (CNN), and to reuse output from several of those capsules to form more stable (with respect to various perturbations) representations for higher capsules. The output is a vector consisting of the probability of an observation, and a pose for that observation. This vector is similar to what is done for example when doing classification with localization in CNNs. Among other benefits, capsnets address the "Picasso problem" in image recognition: images that have all the right parts but that are not in the correct spatial relationship (e.g., in a "face", the positions of the mouth and one eye are switched). For image recognition, capsnets exploit the fact that while viewpoint changes have nonlinear effects at the pixel level, they have linear effects at the part/object level. This can be compared to inverting the rendering of an object of multiple parts.

explainer.lead: A capsule neural network, or CapsNet, is a neural network design for recognizing objects while keeping track of how their parts are arranged. It aims to represent both what has been observed and its pose, helping it avoid treating a scrambled collection of parts as a correctly assembled object.

tiers.eli5: Imagine recognizing a face not just by finding eyes, a nose, and a mouth, but also by checking whether they are in sensible places. A capsule neural network groups information into little teams that pass what they find to bigger teams. This helps it tell a normal face from one where an eye and the mouth have swapped positions.
tiers.practitioner: CapsNets extend convolutional neural networks with capsules whose outputs are reused to build higher-level representations. For vision tasks, the output contains an observation probability and a pose, making the architecture relevant when classification must also preserve spatial relationships. A key consideration is whether the model captures part-to-object arrangement rather than merely detecting all the parts.
tiers.paperLevel: A CapsNet augments a CNN with capsules and reuses outputs from several lower capsules to form higher-capsule representations that are more stable under perturbations. Its output can be written as y = (p, pose), where p is the probability of an observation and pose describes that observation. The design exploits the idea that viewpoint changes are nonlinear at pixel level but linear at the part/object level, although the entry does not establish performance limits.

usedIn.name: Image recognition
usedIn.detail: Used to model part-to-object spatial relationships and address images whose parts are present but incorrectly arranged.

usedIn.name: Classification with localization
usedIn.detail: Its vector output, combining an observation probability with a pose, resembles the information needed when identifying and locating an observation.

components.name: Convolutional neural network
components.detail: Provides the base network to which capsule structures are added.

components.name: Lower capsules
components.detail: Produce outputs representing observations that can be reused by higher-level capsules.

components.name: Higher capsules
components.detail: Combine outputs from several lower capsules into representations intended to remain stable under various perturbations.

components.name: Output vector
components.detail: Contains the probability of an observation together with a pose for that observation.

flow: An observation is processed by the convolutional neural network containing capsule structures.
Several lower capsules produce outputs describing what they have observed.
Those outputs are reused to form more stable representations in higher capsules.
The network emits a vector containing the observation probability and its pose.
explainer.lineage: CapsNets build on convolutional neural networks by adding capsules and drawing inspiration from biological neural organization. They extend part detection with hierarchical spatial relationships, addressing the 'Picasso problem' in which all the right parts are present but incorrectly arranged.
explainer.whyItMatters: Recognizing parts alone can produce false matches when their arrangement is wrong. CapsNets aim to preserve hierarchical and pose information, offering a way to reason about how parts form whole objects as viewpoints and other conditions change.
